title: The Old House

full_text:
On a modern street of tall, new brick buildings stood a venerable old house built three hundred years earlier. Its gables were carved with grinning knights and climbing vines, its leaded windows were narrow, and brass gutters sprouted water-dragons.

Across the street lived a cheerful little boy who loved looking at the picturesque antique building. In the bay window sat an old man with silver hair and knee-breeches, living in solitary retirement.

Feeling that the old gentleman must be lonely, the little boy wrapped one of his precious tin soldiers in paper and sent it across the street with the maid as a present.

The old man was overjoyed by the child's tender thought. He invited the boy to visit the antique home, where gilded leather tapestries whispered stories from the walls, family portraits smiled, and an ancient piano chimed sweet melodies of long-ago days.

The tin soldier lived in the old house, keeping the lonely elder company until the old man passed peacefully away. Years later, when the old house was demolished and a new garden planted, the boy—now a grown man with a loving family—found the rusted tin soldier buried in the earth, and felt his heart fill with gratitude for the timeless lessons of friendship across generations.
moral: Honoring the elderly with youthful kindness brings warmth to lonely years and seeds memories for the future.
